AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agricultural Biotechnology? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agricultural Biotechnology.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Agricultural Biotechnology.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Biotechnology.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agricultural Biotechnology.

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Erosion Control? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Erosion Control.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Erosion Control.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Erosion Control.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Erosion Control.

4. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

5. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Disease control? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Disease control.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Disease control.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Disease control.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Disease control.

7. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Livestock Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Livestock Nutrition.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Livestock Nutrition.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Livestock Nutrition.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Livestock Nutrition.

9. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Breeding? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Breeding.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Breeding.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Breeding.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Breeding.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Forage Crops? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Forage Crops.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Forage Crops.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Forage Crops.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Forage Crops.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Livestock Nutrition and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Breeding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Health: Disease Control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Biotechnology.

2. A — 100 °C

3. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Erosion Control.

4. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

5. B — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Disease control.

7. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

8. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Livestock Nutrition.

9. A — newton (N)

10. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.

11. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Breeding.

12. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Forage Crops.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Livestock Nutrition; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Animal Breeding; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Animal Health: Disease Control; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
